concepts.quote: d = i happens by itself because double is bigger
concepts.why: It gives one correct fact about double having the larger range, but it doesn't trace any values or relate double to another type in more depth.
It correctly says a double becomes an int only through a cast and an int widens to double on its own, but it never says the cast truncates.

concepts.quote: d = i happens by itself because double is bigger; going from 9.99 to int needs (int)
concepts.why: It ties both conversions to the size of each type's range: int to double happens automatically and double to int needs a cast, applied to the lines in this code.
It makes one correct point about types having different ranges, with no trace or wider reasoning about data types.
